imp_text: Biological Magnetic Resonance Data Bank (BMRB) is an archive of NMR data that has evolved for 25 years and served the NMR community through its content and software. The goal of this application is to seek funding to sustain this powerful resource by advancing the content, quality, and distribution, as well as contributing to the development of the Worldwide Protein data Bank (wwwPDB). The PI is the head of BMRB and well qualified to lead the project, and experienced staff scientists have been hired. The research plan claims to aggressively explore novel methods to expand the archive content, improve the data quality and ease the data retrieve process. However, most of the methods in Aim 1 have been established and the large portion of funds will be used to maintain the day-to-day operations. Therefore, the potential innovation would be incremental. Aim 2 is mainly about implementing the recommendations from the wwPDB. It is unclear how many of those are initiated by the PI. To more general users, it is unclear what aspects of BMRB will be useful, and why improvements are needed. The environment for the proposed research is adequate.

imp_text: As conceived the proposal tackles an important area but I have concerns that it would produce results that would have significant impact. The theoretical side is well developed but the experimental validation and feedback seem weak in comparison. The goal seems more to prove a hypothesis rather than test it. The use of small peptides as an experimental system is only briefly described and no information (other than the letter of support) is provided for the lysozyme system also claimed to be used. There were weaknesses in the overall proposal presentation. It was very unusual to see a research paper attached to the proposal, especially given that the reference to the paper was missing. This negatively impacted the argument. Timeline and budget were not detailed. It was unclear why so much effort was put into the model approach (two post-docs and a graduate student) and so little into the validation and feedback (one graduate student) given that a key argument was the lack of experimental data. I do not anticipate this proposal making a large research impact.

study_section: Macromolecular Structure and Function B Study Section
imp_text: This is an outstanding proposal from an early-stage investigator with proven productivity in the area of proposed research.  The proposal has two high-impact specific aims; one suggesting cis-trans isomerization of a specific Proline residue (P624) in the central clock component as the key determinant in switching interaction partners, while the other proposing molecular mimicry as the mechanistic basis for repression of the CLOCK:BMAL1 activity in cells that have undergone cellular transformation.  A detailed analysis of the structural basis of these interactions will not only bridge a critical knowledge gap about how the activator-repressor homeostasis is achieved, but also will lay the foundation for therapeutic intervention that can reset an out of rhythm biological clock.  Since, several disease conditions are known to arise from disruption of the normal clock functioning, the acquired knowledge will be of immense medical significance.  Apart from that, the basic understanding of the mechanism behind long-term regulation of the circadian transcription and translation will advance the field of biological time-keeping to a considerable extent.  The experimental approach is well planned with potential caveats highlighted and alternative roadmaps chalked out.  Indication of strong and enthusiastic collaborative support raises the likelihood of successful completion of the project goals.  Overall the proposal represent an outstanding endeavor with a well thought out roadmap and a promise for long-term scientific gain.
sig_text_str: . The circadian clock coordinates temporal control of physiological processes by global regulation of gene expression on a diurnal cycle.  Interference with which by environmental factors or genetic changes can lead to onset of disease conditions such as diabetes, cardiovascular ailment, premature aging, and cancer. The heterodimeric protein transcription factor CLOCK:BMAL1 occupies a core position in controlling the molecular machinery that synchronizes the circadian clock of body’s biological rhythms to that of the solar cycle.  Understanding the molecular mechanism of its regulation by the co-activators and co-repressors will illuminate on its mode of controlling clock genes. . The circadian clock maintains cellular homeostasis through transcriptional regulation of a significant portion of the genome regulating peak activities of most cellular processes, such as DNA replication/Cell Division and DNA excision repair to specifics times of the day. The CLOCK:BMAL1 protein plays a central role in this oscillating circadian rhythm by switching between its active and repressed conformational states through interaction with global transcriptional regulators (MLL1/CIPC). Identification of the intrinsic factors that orchestrate the transcriptional regulation is crucial for the understanding of the biological timekeeping. . The present work will advance the understanding at the molecular level of the circadian oscillator mechanism and provide a mechanistic model linking disruption of circadian rhythm with incidence of cancer.  The conceptual gain will form the foundation for the treatment of circadian disruption related diseases, in general. . The existing knowledge in the field is limited by the lack of structural data defining the dynamic control mechanism of the CLOCK:BMAL1 heterodimer.  The proposed work will generate a spatial as well as a temporal map of the complex interaction events, at the molecular level, providing future directions in the development of potential therapeutics for prevention of certain chronic diseases including diabetes.

The hypothesis stating cis-trans isomerization of a specific proline residue in the C-TAD domain of the BMAL1 protein induces the key conformational transition that dictates the change in preference for interacting partner is highly innovative and lays a strong scientific foundation for the proposal.  The methodologies to study the two conformations in vitro and at the cellular level are original and well founded. . The idea that a slow conformational transition in the C-TAD domain limits accessibility to activators or repressors is a novel concept, which, if proven, may uncover how protein conformational dynamics can play an important role in tuning long timescale biological events. . NMR spectroscopy is ideal for the study of flexible protein domains. It allows biochemical analysis with atomic resolution.  The proposal takes a balanced approach using NMR spectroscopy and quantitative biochemical analysis to identify the structural dynamics of protein interactions that manipulate CLOCK:BMAL1 transactivation domains to accomplish 24-hour biological timekeeping.

app_text_str: . The proposal intends to define key molecular events that orchestrate the cellular control of biological timekeeping, and extends the study towards understanding the mechanism by which cellular circadian rhythm gets disrupted by endogenous factors under pathological conditions. The mammalian circadian clock is regulated by a transcriptional/translational feedback loop, which has a heterodimeric protein CLOCK:BMAL1 as the central clock component, which regulates expression of the core clock factors through rhythmic changes in histone modification.  The proposal has two main areas of focus; one, to define how energetically costly conformational change in the C-TAD domain of BMAL1 protein leads to regulation of the 24-hour biological rhythm, and the second, determining how cancer-regulated protein uses molecular mimicry to hijack the function of the CLOCK protein transactivation domain Exon 19 in order to manipulate the biological clock. . The Specific Aim 1 takes a structural biology approach to determine how conformational switch in the BMAL1 C-TAD domain determines its differential interaction with activators versus repressors. It has a strong working hypothesis proposing a cis-trans isomerization of a central Pro residue (P625) acting as a switch between two main conformers each with its characteristics interaction affinity for co-activators (CRY1) and co-repressors (p300).  The idea is highly innovative and scientifically sound. . (Aim 1) The solution NMR approach to distinguish the two conformers is solid and proved feasible with preliminary data, and the mutagenesis approach to test its validity in intact cells will validate its functional significance.  State of the art technique ITC will be used for determining the kinetics of binding competition between the co-activator and co-repressor with the WT and trans-locked (P625A mutant) minimal C-TAD, whereas, pull-down assays of Flag-tagged WT and P625A protein will determine the cellular consequences of the trans-locked conformation.  Using cells of BMAL1 -/- background and expressing the mutant using viral expression system will provide convincing results. . Specific Aim 2, is designed to dissect the molecular mechanism by which activator (MLL1) and repressor (CIPC) proteins compete for the same interaction domain Exon 19 in CLOCK to determine the nature of regulatory outcome of the CLOCK:BMAL1 complex on transcriptional activity of the clock genes.  Competition between the activator and repressor maintains the homeostasis of clock gene expression.  The outcome of the molecular dissection will define the way endogenous cellular factor may manipulate the CLOCK:BAML1 activity to set the biological clock out of rhythm leading to chronic diseases. The research aim is based on a novel idea that molecular mimicry may play an active role in this regulation process by proteins that carry structural homology to the Exon 19 domain. The hypothesis is highly innovative and can be successfully tested using the methodology described in the proposal. . (Aim 2) The use of PASD1, a cancer induced clock regulator, for testing this hypothesis takes advantage of a well know endogenous factor known to disturb the rhythmic expression of clock genes, and at the same time adds considerable clinical significance to the experimental outcome. . (Aim 2) The determination of the minimal fragment composition (using ITC and Co-IP) and its structure (using solution NMR) for binding to Exon 19 site will map the structural determinant for stabilizing the highly flexible Exon 19 region into a specific conformation that leads to clock disruption. This will not only advance the understanding of how PASD1 work in cancer cells to manipulate clock gene expression, but also will identify a novel target for therapeutic intervention. . Extension of the study to find out the functional consequence of such regulation by silencing PASD1 in PASD1+ primary cancer cells, as well as in the two PASD1+ human cancer lines with CLOCK-specific reporter, will validate medical relevance of the in vitro findings.

imp_text: BMRB, is a bioinformatics database, which provides invaluable service to the biomedical research community, especially to the structural biologists and biochemists. The ongoing support for the program from NLM is running out due to policy changes, with no promise for further support in the horizon. BMRB is run by a group of highly accomplished scientists and strong collaborative ventures.  The current proposal solicits funding for sustaining BMRB archive and services as well as for developing new tools to advance its mission. The impact of BMRB to the NMR spectroscopists and structural biologists is unquestionable. The mission is of high impact. However, the work described in the proposal is not a hypothesis-driven research project, where the impact of the research can be judged by the novelty of a central hypothesis or by the extent of knowledge advancement.  Therefore, the merit of the proposed research cannot be fairly evaluated using conventional judgment, instead has to be measured in terms of its long-term benefit to the scientific community. The preliminary data reflecting the usefulness of the ongoing service provided by BMRB to the structural biology community is more than convincing, and the defined needs to sustain and improve the technology are well founded.  Therefore, although, as an unsolicited research project, the merit of the proposal ranks in the “Very Good” range (Score: 4), the overall impact would have been outstanding (Score: 2) if the submission were in response to an RFA or a program announcement.
sig_text_str: . BMRB is a repository for experimental and derived data obtained from NMR spectroscopic studies of biological molecules. It is a product of an innovative initiative and continuing involvement from the NMR spectroscopists and computer scientists. It proves to be a valuable resource in the day-to-day research-flow of NMR spectroscopy by acquiring experimental NMR data, developing software to automate and analyze them, helping validate the results of NMR data analysis, and also, by training the new generation of NMR spectroscopists. . Despite its multifaceted impact on the scientific advancement in the field of structural biology, the funding for the project is running out with no indication of new support coming from any governmental institute.  The proposal successfully presents the impact that BMRB currently has on the structural biology research, lists the important services it provide, how those services can be improved, and how new collaborative efforts can be developed to elevate its scope. . The PI appears to be one of the chief administrators of BMRB, who presents a clear vision about what is needed to sustain the resource and how to advance its compatibility with other similar databases, and how to make it make universally acceptable. The facility is run by a group of on-site researchers with appropriate scientific expertize and supported by effective collaborations. . Successful accomplishment of the goals of the project will profoundly improve the usefulness of BMRB and help develop new tools to better interface with other similar databases, such as wwPDB.

The increasing dependency on informatics to facilitate and accelerate discovery in biomedical sciences demands establishment of well-curated databases that acquire, organize, assimilate and disseminate experimental results in a global scale. BMRB is a unique database that acquires information derived from solution- and solid-state NMR spectroscopy and generate tools for streamlining procedures for structure determination of biomolecules using NMR spectroscopic data, and for developing ways to validate as well as improve the quality of the derived structures . BMRB-derived information is particularly useful in structure-function analysis of intrinsically disordered protein domains, determining protein folding energy landscape, improving the robustness of protein structure determination, studying protein-drug interaction and protein-protein interaction.  The BMRB archive remains a key player in the development of methods for calculating structure and structural constraints from NMR chemical shifts and for NMR chemical shift validation tools. .

imp_text: Strength: The proposal intends to study structure-function of a nucleoside transporter from Vibrio cholerae (vCNT) as a model system for understanding the mode of functioning of human homologs hCNTs. Since the role of CNTs in maintaining metabolic balance of cellular nucleoside pool and in transport of nucleoside analogs used as antimicrobials and anticancer drugs is well established, the proposed study will not only advance our basic understanding of a key cellular process, but also may unfold new strategies to develop nucleoside analogs with improved therapeutic potential.  The experimental designing is solid, using well-standardized biochemical and biophysical techniques. The first two specific aims are completely independent of each other, therefore, can progress in parallel.  Specific aim 3 is the most challenging of all, which would combine prior knowledge and data obtained from the first two specific aims for experimental planning, but reasonably well founded from the technical point of view.  Overall, the scientific approach is well thought out that includes state of the art technologies in addressing the central question.  Good contingency plans are in place, in case any of the proposed methodologies fail to yield meaningful data.  The experimental approach is well within the PI’s scientific and technical expertise, without any apparent need for collaboration.  Although there is no new hypothesis around which the proposal is built, the success of the project will significantly advance the field.  In summary, this is an excellent research proposal with a strong chance of success.
sig_text_str: . The hCNTs belong to a larger family of solute transporters SLC28 and are responsible for nucleoside transport in many different tissues.  Several nucleoside-based drugs, including many anticancer compounds, are known to use hCNTs for their passage into healthy as well as malignant cells.  A detailed knowledge of the structure and mechanism of action of these transporters would lay the foundation for rational design of new nucleoside-derived antimicrobial and anticancer drugs with improved tissue delivery and efficacy. . X-ray crystallographic structure determination of the substrate bound and substrate-free transporter will not only help identify the points of physical interaction between the drug substrates and the individual amino acid residues at the active site but also reveal the major conformation changes during transport cycle, which is absolutely critical for defining its mechanism of transport. . Functional studies of the mutants (vCNT and hCNT) using ITC, radioactive uptake assays and fluorescence quenching assay would provide detailed information on the bioenergetics and stoichiometry of transport. The knowledge obtained from the study with vCNT would be utilized in crystalizing and characterizing the human homologs. . Overall, it addresses a basic science question that if successfully answered could bridge a medically relevant problem.  Understanding the molecular mechanism of nucleoside transport by the concentrative nucleoside transporters (CNTs) is absolutely critical to rational design of more potent nucleoside analogs with increased efficacy and for tackling transport-related drug resistance against nucleoside analogs.
sig_text_wkn: . The human hCNTs have additional domains of unknown significance, therefore describing the drug-binding site and defining its mode of functioning based on the knowledge obtained from structure function analysis of a bacterial CNT (vCNT) could be challenging.

The innovation is in combining X-ray crystallography with state of the art biochemical techniques to obtain functionally relevant structural information useful in developing nucleoside analogs with improved bioavailability for anticancer and antimicrobial therapy. . Obtaining structure function information of the bacterial nucleoside transporter (vCNT) and applying that knowledge in crystalizing the core functional domain of the human homolog (hCNT), that is difficult to crystalize with all its domains intact, is somewhat innovative.
inn_text_wkn: . The double mutant cycle studies altering the structure of the nucleoside substrates in parallel to directed mutagenesis of the binding site to determine energetic importance of the ligand interaction is a solid proposal but will be difficult to execute.
app_text_str: . Concentrative nucleoside transporters (CNTs) play an important role in metabolism of nucleic acid, cell signaling and in therapeutic treatment of certain pathological conditions.  The proposal takes the high road of solving the crystal structure of the bacterial homolog (vCNT), plans to construct a detailed structure-function relationship and then use that knowledge in working out the mode of action of the more medically relevant human proteins (hCNTs).  The successful execution of the project will lay the foundation for development of more effective nucleoside-based antimicrobial and anti cancer drugs. . The crystallographic studies are well balanced with appropriately designed biochemical and biophysical experiments to work out the structure-function relationship of the nucleoside- and ion-binding sites, the identity and stoichiometry of the ion-coupling, nucleoside specificity, of vCNT and then extend that knowledge to characterize the human homolog. . The crystallization process is already optimized and cry protection conditions are worked out. A low-resolution crystal of vCNT, already obtained, shows the relative arrangements of the transmembrane helices, and a nucleoside-bound crystal that diffracts at 2.5 Å is also available.  A detailed road map is in place for obtaining crystals of the nucleoside-free conformation.  The atomic structures of vCNT will identify key residues involved in nucleoside and ion binding and provide targets for mutagenesis studies. . Ligand binding will be studied using ITC, which has been well standardized as evident from the preliminary data.  One major achievement of the proposal is the ability to preserve the functional state of vCNT under detergent solubilized condition, allowing meaningful interpretation of the structural data in terms of the functional properties of the transporter. . Based on those conditions, a radioactive flux assay using purified and reconstituted protein has been worked out to study the transport mechanism.  This will enable transport measurement of both nucleoside analogs as well as the movement of couple ion.  Identifying the primary ion to which the secondary transport of nucleosides is coupled to will be a major advancement in the understanding the mechanism.  Potential ion binding residues have been identified and will be targeted for mutagenesis. . Defining the key contact points of the nucleoside substrate will allow rational design of more efficient nucleoside analogs for therapeutic use. Information on the nucleoside-bound and nucleoside-free conformations will help understand the catalytic cycle of the transporter. On the other hand identification of the coupled ion will illuminate on the ionophore sensitiveness of the transport mechanism.

Since hCNTs are the long-term target for developing mechanism-based drugs, a more meaningful plan addressing that issue would have strengthened the proposal.  hCNTs have additional domains the implication of which is not well understood, the strategy for using a truncated version of the protein to mimic the bacterial homolog could miss an important functional component of the transporter. . Using patch-clamping to measure ion permeation through a carrier protein might not yield interpretable data, since the rate of ion flux is way too slow for secondary porters compared to that of ion channels (for which it is the technique of choice).

imp_text: The project aims to uncover the structural mechanism for circadian rhythm regulation, specifically the molecule interactions with CLOCK:BMAL1 and its flexible C-TAD domain. This work would provide a structural perspective of key activation event, namely a conformational “switch” induced by a cis-trans proline isomerization. The overall methods to be used are appropriate for direct observation of this event on a micro- to millisecond timescale and for mapping minimalistic binding sites for other regulators to CLOCK:BMAL1. If successful, the proposal may elucidate a structural mechanism linking circadian misregulation and somatic cancer. However, the proposal lacks clear milestones and quantifiable criteria for success, does not sufficiently justify the impact of the work other than a general corollary with cancer, and does not justify the requested funds. Overall, the project will have a marked positive impact on the circadian regulation field.
sig_text_str: . Diseases affecting large groups within the population (e.g. diabetes, cardiovascular disease, cancer) are linked to circadian misregulation. . Currently the structural mechanism of a key regulator (CLOCK:BMAL1) is unknown. . The proposed work to elucidate the structural dynamics of CLOCK:BMAL1 regulation will begin to describe the structure-function relationship for circadian regulation. . The work will benefit from the PI’s previously determined crystal structure of CLOCK:BMAL1. . A better understanding of the structural interactions of CLOCK:BMAL1 with PER, CRY, and the PASD1 mimic may provide insight for new/complimentary therapies for the aforementioned complex diseases. . From end of Aim 2: “We expect that by doing do, we will highlight novel points for intervention by small molecules to modulate clock timing or reinforce oscillator robustness in human cancer.”
sig_text_wkn: . More detail about previous approaches to therapeutically target CLOCK:BMAL1 would provide better context on their strengths/weaknesses and how structure-based hypotheses may have improved their outcome. . If there have been no attempts, it is important to describe how one would attempt to create a therapeutic using the basic research in this proposal. Given what is currently known, what is the best target? . Assuming the proposed work is successful, it is difficult to ascertain the practicality of the results by other cancer researchers other than “it will be clear once a structural mechanism is known.” . Is it known whether re-establishing a circadian rhythm can have a therapeutic effect on cancer, etc. or is it known to only reduce long-term risks?
inv_text_str: . PI has practical experience with cross-disciplinary approaches to combine cell biology, biochemistry, and structural biology. . PI has practical experience with researching the molecular basis of circadian function. Collaborators have expertise with the target system and will provide materials and/or experimental validation of structural hypotheses. . PI’s group can perform all gold-standard circadian assays in-house.

Approach uses complementary assays (reporter, co-IP, etc.) to test structure-based mechanisms from both aims. . Full-length constructs will be secured if truncated proteins do not achieve their intended effect in cell culture. . Potential problems are addressed and alternative approaches are reasonable.
app_text_wkn: . Proposal stops short of solving protein complex structures with C-TAD and instead aims to identify the minimal binding site. Although PI has applied NMR to this type of task, is it indeed the most cost-effective tool for solving the problem? Site-directed mutation perturbation coupled with their existing assays could achieve a similar result. Is NMR the best approach or just the one the PI favors? . Much effort is spent identifying minimal binding motifs, afterwards structural studies seemed focused on peptide interactions. While these motifs may be sufficient for binding, they are arguably too far removed from larger domain constructs or full-length proteins and can lead to a limited structural representation of the protein complexes under investigation. This leads to an increased risk during in vitro studies with full-length constructs. . The criteria for success are not clear and quantifiable. Most read as “Determine a property/mechanism.” How is it determined whether work toward an aim is successful or not? What level of accuracy/significance is acceptable?

study_section: Macromolecular Structure and Function D Study Section
imp_text: The project aims to extend the computational capabilities of the BMRB by including emerging technologies to extract higher-level information from experimental NMR, incorporate experimental and simulated descriptions of structural dynamics, and to improve the process of standardizing and depositing highly-variable experimental NMR data from researchers and to access that detailed data for future use. This represents a special application where the main budget request is for day-to-day operations of the BMRB. Some new structural biology research is proposed to address the open issue of quantifying NMR-based structure quality; however, much of the proposal focuses on integrating existing gold standard NMR analysis software to provide a more holistic view of the deposited data. That being said, the letters of support clearly demonstrate that BMRB is a critical resource to the worldwide NMR community and its dissolution would result in a field-wide loss of productivity, hinder experimental reproducibility, and ultimately lead to wasted effort where the nature of the data becomes ephemeral as technology and techniques advance. The research team has abundant expertise and experience in NMR research and software development to carry out the project. Overall, the project will exert a significantly high impact on the field.
sig_text_str: . NMR has the ability to directly observe different types of structural dynamics. . Characterizing and understanding protein flexibility/plasticity/dynamics is a critical part of understanding the structure-function relationship for a biopolymer. . BMRB is already a valuable and indispensable resource for structural biologist, collecting and curating NMR spectral data, and has an existing global user base. . Many scientific software programs have been developed using or rely on BMRB-hosted data. . Loss of the services provided by BMRB will be detrimental to the structural biology community. . Structure quality metrics to describe the strengths and limitations of an NMR structure for the average biologist are sorely needed.

Outreach efforts with NMR community to ensure higher quality and more complete deposition data.
inn_text_wkn: . Key software innovation is being developed by partners and other groups. . Funding is for BMRB day-to-day operations. . Main innovation appears to be in the form of a single warehouse for data collection, primary analysis, and distribution. Having many software tools is useful, but there could be more innovative uses of them in concert. The single example described in some detail is the deposition system.
app_text_str: . NMR-STAR data format is extensible, allowing adaptation as new types of data are recorded. . Automated methods using GeoDeepDive to extract NMR-relevant metadata from manuscripts will decrease manual maintenance of BMRB records and assist users when depositing data. . Qualitative metrics are proposed to judge the utility of literature data extraction techniques. . Workflows can be supported for multiple user groups: graphical analysis for end users, web interfaces for developers. . Automating basic validation inquiries so that depositions can be more quickly validated at the partner wwPDB website, which provides faster feedback about errors to depositors for correction. . More complete automatic annotation to characterize whether regions are well or ill-defined, and the extended ability to characterize whether ill-defined regions are due to disorder/flexibility or experimental error. . Back-calculation of NOE peaks is similar to crystallographic approach to calculation error with calculated diffraction patterns from structure models.
app_text_wkn: . “Innovative techniques for obtaining experimental data and metadata will be explored…” The proposed techniques and enhancements are not defined. . It is not clear what constitutes success even though some qualitative metrics. Metric thresholds defining success are needed. . Aim 1 proposes the creation and maintenance of related but independent services for the BMRB web site, each with value. It is not described how these services provide a greater value than “the sum of their parts.” How will they interact with one another? Is it the Hohm collaboration for deposition is the only example to be exploited? Are there additional case studies to be presented? . Proposal comes short of constructing NMR structure quality and similarity metrics as suggested in significance.

study_section: Biochemistry and Biophysics of Membranes Study Section
imp_text: The project aims to uncover the structural mechanism for nucleoside transport across a lipid membrane, specifically through biophysical analysis of a prokaryotic concentrative nucleoside transporter (CNT). This work would provide a structural perspective of the transportation of nucleoside-based therapeutics—a difficult challenge due to the fact the target is an integral membrane protein. There exists a critical need for more experimental effort to solve the structures of this difficult protein class and the PI is well qualified to address this topic. The fact that NT deactivation has already been identified as the source of drug resistance in some cases establishes a clear link that, if successful, a biophysical functional analysis of CNTs will aid in designing a solution around this resistant. A mediated risk, but a concern none the less, is the proposed use of the Vibrio cholera CNT (vcCNT) as a homolog for the human CNTs (hCNT) given that the PI reports only a 40% sequence identity between the two. Structural fold similarity can be observed with as little as 5% ID; however, homology modeling is typically safest when used above 50% ID, preferably 70%. Uridine binding and uridine transport activity is observed between the two, which suggests vcCNT and hCNT may be similar enough to achieve the goals of the structural studies. However, by the proposed schedule, it will take 24 months just to answer this question. The proposal lacks clear milestones and quantifiable criteria for success. This reviewer would like to see a more focused discussion on the direct steps and criteria required to answer this fundamental hypothesis in a shorter time frame. Overall, the project will exert a high impact on the understanding of nucleoside-based drug transport and add to the knowledgebase of membrane protein crystallography.
sig_text_str: . Project centers on determining the structure-based mechanism for active transport of nucleosides across a membrane, an essential part of nucleoside physiology. . Nucleoside-based drug therapies against cancer and viruses are transported by the same mechanism. Drug resistance has been linked to transport deficiencies. . No structures of the CNT class exist to date. . Preliminary structure studies exist for vcCNT, a proposed model system for understanding hCNT. . Basic uridine binding and transport has been demonstrated in vcCNT and hCNT. . Project will also determine the specificity of transport for nucleosides and derivative drugs, which can help determine new drug designs to counter drug resistance.
sig_text_wkn: . Project aims are significantly limited, but not extinguished, if an atomic-level vcCNT structure is not determined or vcCNT is not a “homologous enough” model system.
inv_text_str: . PI has practical experience and expertise in the structure determination of other integral membrane proteins. . PI has practical experience with port/transport flux assays and has already successfully applied it to the proposed model system. . PI’s group has the internal and department resources required to perform all proposed assays in-house.
inn_text_str: . Project would produce the first experimental atomic-level structure of a CNT, which is expected to have a novel structural fold. . Utilization of an in vitro flux/uptake assay provides a new level of control when dissecting the mechanism of a CNT. . Expects to determine the residue-level binding site for a CNT for the first time. . Builds upon previous success in characterizing the structure-based function of integral membrane pores.
inn_text_wkn: . The approaches proposed are similar to those used by the PI in other contexts. This does reduce the risk of the proposal, but slightly tempers the innovation of the work. . The PI constructs the Innovation section exceedingly brief. Reviewers can synthesize the importance of this proposal on their own; however, the relative inattention given to this section is surprising given the importance that NIH grant guidelines place on it.
app_text_str: . For crystallization studies, vcCNT crystals that diffract and are used to create a 4.5 Å model exist. . Several alternate methods for improving phasing have been proposed. Reasonable evidence on their applicability to integral membrane proteins has been presented. . Planned apo/holo structures are essential for characterizing potential induced-conformational changes. . Oligomeric status experiments appear appropriate to determine the stoichiometry of the CNT biological assembly. . Much of the proposed functional studies can be achieved in the absence of an atomic structure of vcCNT. . The proposed double-mutant cycle experiments seem critical for dissecting the mechanism of drug transport specificity in vcCNT/hCNTs. . Given a successfully determined atomic-level structure of vcCNT and validation that vcCNT is an appropriate model system for hCNT, it is quite plausible that this proposal will create an intricately-detailed mechanism of nucleoside transport that can be exploit for improvements to existing nucleoside-based drug therapies.
app_text_wkn: . Since an “everything but the kitchen sink” approach to improving phasing has been suggested, is there a reason that cubic phase approaches (Landau & Rosenbusch, 1996) are left out? They have been successfully applied to GPCRs. . Structure-guided functional characterization of hCNT hinges on traditional homology modeling (use of MODELLER and SWISS-MODEL specifically). Given the relatively low sequence identity (40% ID), there is a reasonable chance of failure; especially if a target-template alignment is not accurate. Alternate algorithms that utilize protein threading and ab initio-styled techniques (I-TASSER, MULTICOM, and other top-ranking CASP competition entries) may be critical to successful modeling efforts. . Clear milestones and criteria for success are not discussed. It is extremely difficult to predict whether the proposed project timeline is accurate or feasible without this information. . Mutational studies without an atomic structure are predicated that three glutamate residues are conserved between hCNTs and vcCNT, but what about other species? A broader sampling that demonstrates the conservation at these positions would support the expectation of a higher degree of success for these studies. . I would like to see more focus on correlating how the context of the functional and specificity analyses correlate with the variability observed in known drug resistant hCNTs. This topic could be constructed into a putative criterion for success.
env_text_str: . PI lab and departmental resources are complete to accomplish the proposed work. . PI leads an active protein crystallography group, which possess the specialties and basic reagents/equipment needed for X-ray crystollgraphy.
